purpose: Measure what a two-tier operating point delivers on the frozen baseline: an alert tier whose threshold is chosen for precision on the prior calibration year, and a watch tier that keeps the project operating point of config/operating-point-v2.json (prior calibration year, window recall 0.90). Decision aid for redefining the project target. No model, feature or probability changes; zero fits.
why: Ten routes left precision at the recall-0.90 operating point in the 0.04-0.21 band, and accuracy below the always-negative accuracy in every year. Accuracy above always-negative is equivalent to precision above 0.50 (TP greater than FP). The baseline's evaluation-year oracle reaches precision 0.50 only at recall 0.48 (2014), 0.48 (2015), 0.33 (2016), 0.80 (2017), 0.15 (2022) and 0.07 (2023). The question is what a prior-year precision rule delivers, since the oracle is not deployable.
arm: baseline (original 96-summary ensemble), stage-one inference only with the stored frozen models; zero fits

watch.rule: helio24.calibration.recall_threshold on the prior calibration year at window recall 0.90; must reproduce the stored 0.9 threshold of the watch_tier_thresholds file bit for bit.

alert.rule: helio24.two_tier.precision_threshold on the prior calibration year: among candidate thresholds of helio24.modeling.threshold_curve whose calibration-year window recall is at least the recall floor, take those whose calibration-year window precision is at least the precision target and choose the one with the highest recall (ties: lowest threshold). If no candidate reaches the target, choose the candidate with the highest precision (ties: highest recall, then lowest threshold) and mark the year as fallback.
alert.recall_floor_reason: A threshold that alarms on a handful of calibration windows is a count fluke, not a rule; 0.10 of the calibration-year positive windows is the smallest set judged stable before any result was seen.

intervals: helio24.calibration.cluster_intervals, full-HARP bootstrap, 1000 draws, seed 24, on evaluation-year windows at the chosen threshold.
oracle: For each precision target, the highest evaluation-year recall at which any threshold reaches it (scripts.audit_operating_point.recall_for_precision). Not deployable; an upper bound only.
order_of_operations: Thresholds for both tiers, all targets and all years are written to disk and hashed before any evaluation label is read.

reading.year_meets_primary: alert tier at the primary target delivers evaluation-year precision >= 0.50, which is the same as accuracy above the always-negative accuracy, and is not a fallback year
reading.redefinition_supported_if: year_meets_primary holds in at least four of six years and the watch tier is identical to the operating-point-v2 result in every year
reading.meaning: Support justifies writing config/operating-point-v3.json with the two tiers for development reporting. It never changes alerts, dashboard thresholds or models; the reserved 2024-2025 test stays closed.

scope: Adaptive development description on already inspected years, not an independent test. Counts are overlapping forecast windows and groupings of them, not physical flares. Precision at a low-recall tier is measured on few alarm windows in quiet years and its interval must be read with the point.
prohibitions: No new precision targets, recall floors or tie rules after seeing results
No presentation of an oracle point as deployable
